record.paper_title: On some open problems of number theory
record.context_brief: von Koch form of the Riemann hypothesis
record.original_question: Let pi(x) count the primes at most x, and let li(x) denote the logarithmic integral. Does there exist a constant A such that every positive x satisfies |pi(x) - li(x)| < A sqrt(x) log x?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a real number $x>0$, let $\pi(x)$ denote the number of prime numbers not exceeding $x$, and let $\mathrm{li}(x) = \int_0^x \frac{dt}{\log t}$ (interpreted as a Cauchy principal value at $t=1$) denote the logarithmic integral. Determine whether there exists an absolute constant $A>0$ such that
$$|\pi(x) - \mathrm{li}(x)| < A\,\sqrt{x}\,\log x \qquad \text{for every } x>0\text{ (equivalently, for every } x\ge 2\text{)}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The inequality $|\pi(x) - \mathrm{li}(x)| < A\sqrt{x}\log x$ is the classical von Koch form of the Riemann Hypothesis: Helge von Koch (1901) proved it is equivalent to RH. Since the Riemann Hypothesis remains unproved as of 2026, this statement is open.

status_evidence.title: Riemann hypothesis - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Helge von Koch (1901) proved that the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the bound |pi(x) - li(x)| = O(sqrt(x) log x).
status_evidence.claim: The bound is equivalent to RH, which is unresolved.
